newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS - Mystery buyers boost Winterthur.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Mystery buyers boost Winterthur.

text.p: A two day surge in the shares of Winterthur Insurance Company, which jumped seven percent at one stage on Wednesday, has left the market none the wiser about who the buyers are.
"I cannot make sense of this based on fundamentals," Thomas Kalbermatten at Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS ) in Zurich said.
"Somebody out there knows something, but who, and how do they know it, and what do they know?" said Bank Baer analyst Beat Alpiger.

Winterthur spiked around seven percent in afternoon trade on the Swiss bourse before slipping back to close at 1,420 Swiss francs, up 1.2 percent or 16 francs from a close on Tuesday that was itself five percent up from the day before.
The share has gained 8.5 percent this week and 42 percent since breaking 1,000 francs in late March. It has risen over 80 percent since starting the year at 774 francs.

Gains have been driven in part by improved estimates of Winterthur's performance, by a bullish Swiss market and by weeks of vague rumours of some kind of merger in the Swiss financial services sector.

Asked about the five-percent jump on Tuesday, Winterthur's finance officer Erwin Heri told the Swiss business paper Finanz und Wirtschaft it was "the last twitches" of an excited stock market before an eventual correction.
Winterthur believed the two-day surge was excessive, spokeswoman Anna-Marie Kappeler said.
"The most important message is that in our view there is a great deal of fanatasy in these prices. They are really a bit irrational" she said.
"We have no plans for any substantial changes," Kappeler said.
She declined to comment when asked whether Winterthur was facing a take-over bid.
"This is speculation and we do not comment on speculation," she said.

She also declined to say who had been buying the registered shares recently but noted that it normally takes a few days to enter new purchases in the share register, so that buyers from the past two days would not be known to the company yet.
UBS's Kalbermattern noted that Swiss financier Martin Ebner had taken a 15 percent stake in Winterthur earlier this year and might be trying to increase it.
Kalbermatten also said there were companies in Europe with enough financial power to take over Winterthur, even though the price has become very high.
"In the end the question is where an acquiring company sees potential for rationalisation, synergies and so on," he said.
Ebner's BZ Group declined to comment on whether it was raising its stake in Winterthur.
Group board member Kurt Schiltknecht said the group would report its current Winterthur holding at a news briefing for financial journalists set for late on Thursday.
